title: Integrated security & compliance playbook: RBAC, Audit, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence & Risk Exceptions
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates security and compliance practices across RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response (security procedures), compliance evidence workflows, and risk/exception handling. It is intended for engineers, product owners, security reviewers, and auditors.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood Inference production and pre-production environments, associated cloud accounts, and on-prem packages.
- Covers people, process, and technology controls for authentication, authorization, logging, data lifecycle, software development, incident handling, and evidence collection.

1) Ownership and governance

- Primary owner: Security (security@redwood-inference.internal).
- Day-to-day owners: Platform Security (owner: Marco Ruiz), SRE (owner: Jenna Lee), CI/CD & DevEx (owner: Priya Natarajan).
- Compliance steering committee: security, legal, engineering leadership, and product compliance lead — meets monthly.
- Audit and evidence contact: compliance-ops@redwood-inference.internal.

2) RBAC & Authentication

Principles:
- Least privilege by default.
- Role-based access with short-lived elevated sessions (no permanent admin where possible).
- Identity-first: centralize in IAM (cloud IAM + Okta for SSO).

Roles and role definitions (summary table):

| Role | Purpose | Typical Groups | Permissions (examples) | Review cadence |
|------|---------|----------------|------------------------|----------------|
| Platform-Admin | Manage infra, accounts, networking | platform-admins | Full account-level admin, network, VPC | Quarterly |
| Runtime-Operator | Manage runtime clusters, model routing | runtime-ops | Deploy, scale, rollback services | Monthly |
| SRE-Read | Monitoring/triage | sre-read | Read-only access to metrics/logs/dashboards | Quarterly |
| Dev-Committer | App engineers | eng-committer | Code push, deploy to dev/staging | Semi-annually |
| Compliance-Viewer | Audit & compliance reviews | compliance-view | Read-only access to evidence buckets & reports | Quarterly |

Access request and approval workflow:
1. Engineer requests role via Access Request Portal (link: /access-requests).
2. Requestor provides justification, duration, and owner.
3. Manager approval required; for privileged roles, Security approval required.
4. Access is provisioned with an expiry (default 7 days for elevation).
5. Access reviews executed on schedule (see 'Review cadence' column).

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Process: Submit emergency access ticket (pagerduty: Security On-Call) with business justification, required end time.
- All emergency access must be logged, approved post-facto by Security, and followed by a root cause and mitigation note in the ticket.

Authentication configuration highlights:
- SSO: Okta with SCIM provisioning; MFA required for all accounts (hardware + app-based recommended).
- Service principals: use short-lived tokens from Vault; long-lived keys are prohibited unless approved by Security and rotated every 30 days.
- Example CLI to list role bindings (GCP): gcloud iam roles list --project ${PROJECT_ID} --format=json

3) Audit logging

Goals:
- Ensure availability, integrity, and discoverability of logs for detection, investigation, and compliance evidence.

Log sources and retention policy (summary):
- Auth logs (Okta): retention 2 years (retention bucket: s3://redwood-logs-auth-2y, KMS: projects/redwood/kms/auth-key).
- Cloud audit logs (GCP/AWS controlplane): retention 1 year in hot store, 7 years archived (glacier/nearline).
- Application access and admin actions: retention 3 years for compliance scopes.
- Runtime traces & metrics: retention 90 days in Datadog, 7 years aggregated metrics summary.

Logging architecture:
- Agents: Fluentd/Fluent Bit forwards app logs to a central logging pipeline (Kafka -> log-store -> Datadog/Splunk + long-term S3 archive).
- Integrity: all logs are write-once to object store with bucket-level WORM policy for compliance-critical streams. Logs are signed (SHA256) and checksums stored in the evidence service.

Alerting and detection thresholds (examples):
- 5 failed privileged API token uses within 15 minutes -> P1 alert to security-oncall.
- New IAM policy with admin:* created -> P1 alert.
- Anomalous geographic login (new country) for admin user -> P2 alert and temporary session freeze pending review.

Audit access and reviews:
- Compliance-Viewer group has read-only access to evidence buckets via ticket.
- Monthly audit exercises run by compliance to validate logging completeness and integrity.

Example query (Datadog/Splunk):
- Splunk: index=auth sourcetype=okta action=failure | stats count by user, src_ip | where count > 5

4) Data residency and retention

Data classification:
- Public: Documentation, blog posts. Retention: as needed.
- Internal: Operational configs, runbooks. Retention: 3 years.
- Confidential: Customer-provided data, PII, secrets. Retention: per contract and regulation (see table).

Residency mapping (by product/data type):
| Data type | Default region | Storage location | Retention | Notes |
|-----------|----------------|------------------|----------|-------|
| Customer model artifacts | Customer-specified (US/EU/APAC) | Object store (regional) | As per customer contract (min 90 days) | Customers can request deletion/transfer |
| PII (support tickets) | Customer region | Encrypted DB (regional) | 7 years or per DSR | DSR process in section 6 |
| Backups | Multi-region | Encrypted backup vault | 90 days hot, 7 years cold if required by contract |

Data deletion and DSR (Data Subject Request) process:
1. Submit DSR to privacy@redwood-inference.internal (link to DSR intake form).
2. Privacy verifies identity and scope.
3. Data owner executes removal workflow (delete from primary DB, invalidate cache, delete from backups per retention exception policy).
4. Evidence of deletion is recorded and returned to requestor within SLA (30 days for standard DSR).

Cross-border transfers and controls:
- For customer-requested residency, enforce control plane and data plane separation. Keys stored in region-specific KMS where required.
- SCCs and standard contractual clauses are used for transfers where applicable. Legal must be looped for new territories.

5) Secure SDLC

Phases and mandatory controls:
- Plan: Threat model and privacy impact assessment (PIA) required for changes impacting customer data or model behavior.
- Develop: Code reviews (2 approvers for privileged repos), SCA (Dependabot / Snyk), linting, and unit tests.
- Build: CI runs SCA, unit tests, integration tests, and secret scanning. Build artifacts are signed.
- Release: Release gating with canary approvals, automated rollout with rollback playbooks.
- Operate: Runtime monitoring, periodic dependency scanning, quarterly pentests.

Pre-merge gates (example checklist):
- No plaintext secrets in diff.
- At least one approver from a different team for infra changes.
- CI must pass: tests >= 95% coverage for critical modules, SCA alerts resolved or documented.

Secrets handling:
- Use Vault for secrets; never check secrets into repo. CI uses short-lived secrets injected at runtime.
- Example: read secret in CI: VAULT_TOKEN=$(vault login -method=github role=ci-role -field=token)

Third-party risk and supply-chain controls:
- All new third-party services must be entered into the third-party registry and reviewed by Risk & Legal.
- Critical dependencies must have observed security posture (CVE triage cadence: 72 hours for critical, 7 days for high).

6) Incident response (security procedures)

Severity levels and SLAs:
- Sev 0 (P0): Active intrusion or data exfiltration confirmed -> mitigation in 1 hour, full incident briefing in 4 hours.
- Sev 1 (P1): Privileged credential compromise or breach-like events -> mitigation in 4 hours, initial report in 8 hours.
- Sev 2 (P2): Elevated suspicious activity -> investigation started within 24 hours.

Security incident steps (high level):
1. Triage & contain: SIRT on-call takes ownership, isolates affected resources (network quarantine, token revocation).
2. Preserve evidence: Snapshot disk, export logs (immutable copies), preserve memory captures if needed.
3. Investigate: Forensics team performs root cause analysis; timeline and IOC (indicators of compromise) documented.
4. Remediate: Patch, revoke credentials, rotate keys, apply compensating controls.
5. Communicate: Internal comms (Slack #security-incidents), external comms coordinated with Legal and Comms.
6. Post-incident review: Postmortem within 7 business days; remedial actions tracked in JIRA with owners and due dates.

Forensic evidence preservation checklist:
- Record all commands run by investigators.
- Time-sync all artifacts (use UTC).
- Store evidence in evidence-bucket with WORM and checksum.
- Maintain chain-of-custody log (who accessed evidence and when).

7) Compliance evidence workflows

Principles:
- Single source of truth for evidence (evidence service + S3 buckets with metadata tags).
- Ownership: each control has an evidence owner responsible for maintaining artifacts.
- Automation first: automate evidence capture where possible (CI artifacts, logging exports, access reviews).

Evidence run cadence (examples):
- SOC 2 Type II: Continuous collection with quarterly internal readiness reviews and annual external audit.
- GDPR: Data processing records updated on change; DSR evidence maintained per request.

Common evidence types and owners (summary):
| Evidence artifact | Owner | Storage location | Retention |
|-------------------|-------|------------------|----------|
| Access review reports | HR / Security | s3://evidence/access-reviews | 7 years |
| Pen test reports | Security | s3://evidence/pen-tests | 7 years |
| Change approvals (prod deploys) | Eng-Release | s3://evidence/deploy-audit | 3 years |
| Runtime config snapshots | Runtime-Ops | s3://evidence/runtime-configs | 3 years |

Automated evidence capture examples:
- CI: upload signed build artifacts and test reports to evidence bucket upon merge.
- Access reviews: scheduled exports from Okta into evidence store (monthly).
- Logging integrity: store log checksums in evidence service after each archive job.

Audit preparation runbook (summary):
1. For scope selection, pull control list from the audit request.
2. Run evidence-gathering script: ./tools/gather-evidence --control-file controls.csv --out /tmp/audit-evidence.
3. Package artifacts and create an evidence ticket for auditor access.
4. Notify compliance lead and schedule walkthrough.

8) Risk & exceptions

Exceptions process:
1. Submit exception request with justification, risk assessment, compensating controls, and proposed duration.
2. Security reviews and either approves, conditionally approves (with controls), or denies.
3. Approved exceptions are time-boxed (max 90 days) and assigned an owner for remediation.
4. Exceptions are tracked in the Risk Register and reviewed monthly by the steering committee.

Risk matrix (summary):
- Low: local dev convenience, minimal customer impact. Acceptable with owner remediation in 90 days.
- Medium: internal tooling or non-prod data exposure. Requires compensating control and 60-day remediation.
- High: production customer data access or admin privilege changes. Requires executive sign-off and 30-day remediation or immediate rollback.

Compensating controls examples:
- Increased monitoring & alerting, network segmentation, temporary MFA escalation, additional logging retention.

9) Reporting, metrics, and continuous improvement

Key metrics to track:
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) security incidents (target < 1 hour for P0/P1).
- Mean time to remediate (MTTR) for P0/P1 (target < 4 hours for P0).
- Percent of infra with automated evidence capture (target 95%).
- Age of open exceptions in the register (target 0 > 90 days).

Continuous improvement cadence:
- Quarterly tabletop exercises for incident response.
- Bi-annual red-team / blue-team exercises for high-risk services.
- Monthly control effectiveness reviews tied to evidence and audit findings.

Appendix: commands and quick references

- Revoke all active tokens for a user (example, Vault): vault lease revoke -prefix auth/token/user/${USER_ID}
- Export Okta login history (example API): curl -H "Authorization: SSWS ${OKTA_TOKEN}" https://your-org.okta.com/api/v1/logs?limit=1000 > okta-logs.json
- Evidence gather script (CI): ./tools/gather-evidence --controls all --dest s3://evidence/audit-exports/${AUDIT_DATE}

Contacts
- Security On-call (PagerDuty): Security-Oncall (see internal rota)
- Compliance Ops: compliance-ops@redwood-inference.internal
- Privacy / DSR: privacy@redwood-inference.internal
